package_info.why_malicious: These packages impersonate legitimate IP utility libraries but contain heavily obfuscated JavaScript that, upon import, downloads and executes OS-specific trojan and info-stealer binaries from a hardcoded remote server (95.216.251.178). The packages are part of a coordinated typosquatting campaign targeting developers, resulting in remote code execution and potential data exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code determines the operating system, downloads an OS-specific binary from 95.216.251.178 over HTTP, writes it to the /tmp directory, and executes it using child_process.exec, resulting in immediate remote code execution and potential info-stealing or trojan activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and embedded in a utility library, yet it downloads and executes a remote binary without user consent. Hardcoded external IP addresses and OS detection logic are clear signs of malicious intent, as legitimate IP utility libraries do not require such behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A normal IP utility library should only perform local IP address parsing or make simple HTTP requests to public IP services for geolocation. It should never download or execute binaries, nor contain obfuscated code or hardcoded external endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated updaters or installers may download and execute binaries, but this is never appropriate in a utility library context, especially without explicit user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript code in core utility files (ip.js, in.js)
Hardcoded external IP address (95.216.251.178) for payload delivery
OS detection logic to select and download platform-specific payloads
Writes downloaded binary to /tmp and executes it via child_process.exec
Network activity to non-standard IPs during package import

attack_chain.action: User installs or imports the malicious package, triggering execution of obfuscated code at import-time.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of an OS-specific malicious binary from a hardcoded remote server.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads a trojan/info-stealer binary from 95.216.251.178 based on the user's operating system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the downloaded binary on the victim's machine, enabling arbitrary code execution.

attack_chain.action: The downloaded binary (e.g., svchost.exe, gsd-mouse, node) is executed, performing info-stealing, trojan, or cryptocurrency stealing activities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of the victim's system and exfiltration of sensitive data to the attacker's infrastructure.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript present in utility modules (e.g., ip.js, in.js)
Import-time or install-time code that downloads and executes remote binaries
OS detection logic (os.platform()) followed by network requests to hardcoded IPs
Creation and execution of non-standard binaries in temporary directories (/tmp, %TEMP%)
file_indicators: Downloaded binaries named svchost.exe, gsd-mouse, node in /tmp or %TEMP%
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to 95.216.251.178 during package import or install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan npm packages for obfuscated JavaScript that performs OS detection and downloads executables from hardcoded IP addresses. Flag any package that writes and executes binaries during import or install, especially in utility libraries. Monitor for network connections to 95.216.251.178 or similar suspicious endpoints initiated by Node.js processes. Alert on unexpected process creation from Node.js in the context of package usage, particularly when binaries are written to and executed from temporary directories.
